p: priests: He speaks mainly to them, but under them he includes the people also.
unto my name: To serve me according to my word.
blessings: That is, the abundance of God's benefits.
your seed: The seed you sow will come to no profit.
dung of your solemn feasts: You boast of your holiness, sacrifices, and feasts, but they will turn to your shame and be as vile as dung.

sent this commandment unto you: The Priests objected against the Prophet that he could not remove them without speaking against the priesthood, and the office established by God by promise. But he shows that the office is nothing slandered, when these villains and dung are called by their own names.

covenant was with him of life: He shows what were the two conditions of the covenant made with the tribe of Levi on God's part, that he would give them long life and felicity, and on their part, that they should faithfully serve him according to his word.
gave them to him for the: I commanded Levi a certain law to serve me.
my name: He served me and set forth my glory with all humility and submission.
truth was in his mouth: He shows that the priests ought to have knowledge to instruct others in the word of the Lord.
lips should keep knowledge: He is as the treasure house of God's word, and ought to give to everyone according to their need, and not to reserve it for himself.
messenger of the LORD of hosts: Showing that whoever does not declare God's will, is not his messenger, and priest.

father: The Prophet accuses the ingratitude of the Jews toward God and man: for seeing they were all born of one father Abraham, as God had elected them to be his holy people, they ought neither to offend God nor their brethren.
our fathers: By which they had bound themselves to God to be a holy people.
daughter of a strange god: They have united themselves in marriage with those that are of another religion.
offereth an offering unto the LORD: That is, the priest.
covering the altar of the LORD: Yet cause the people to lament, because God does not regard their sacrifices, so that they seem to sacrifice in vain.
Wherefore: This is another fault, of which he accuses them, that is, that they broke the laws of marriage.
companion: As the one half of yourself.
covenant: She that was united to you by a solemn covenant, and by the invocation of God's name.
he make one: Did not God make man and woman as one flesh and not many?
residue of the spirit: By his power and strength he could have made many women for one man.
seed: Those who should be born in lawful and moderate marriage, in which is no excess of lusts.
spirit: Contain yourselves within your bounds, and be sober in mind, and bridle your affections.
hateth putting away: Not that he allows divorce, but of two faults he shows which is the less.
violence with his garment: He thinks it sufficient to keep his wife still, even though he takes others, and so as it were covers his fault.
wearied the LORD with your words: You murmur against God, because he did not hear you as soon as you called.
evil is good in the sight: In thinking that God favoured the wicked, and had no respect for those that serve him.
judgment: Thus they blasphemed God in condemning his power and justice, because he did not judge according to their imaginings.
